scenario: A geospatial intelligence agency recruits analysts who demonstrate expert multi-spectral image analysis OR advanced GIS spatial reasoning. Both skills are independent in the candidate pool; OR-gate selection produces negative within-analyst correlation.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (multi-spectral image analysis) OR (GIS spatial reasoning)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(spectral_analysis | ¬gis_reasoning, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(spectral_analysis | gis_reasoning, selected) and show it equals P(spectral_analysis). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between multi-spectral image analysis and GIS spatial reasoning.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks GIS spatial reasoning must possess multi-spectral image analysis to be admitted — hence P(spectral_analysis|¬gis_reasoning,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has GIS spatial reasoning is admitted regardless of multi-spectral image analysis, so P(spectral_analysis|gis_reasoning,sel)=P(spectral_analysis)=0.34. The gap (1.0 vs 0.34) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between multi-spectral image analysis and GIS spatial reasoning observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.34+0.46-0.34×0.46=0.6436. (2) Among candidates without GIS spatial reasoning: only those with multi-spectral image analysis are selected → P(spectral_analysis|¬gis_reasoning,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with GIS spatial reasoning: selected regardless of multi-spectral image analysis → P(spectral_analysis|gis_reasoning,sel)=P(spectral_analysis)=0.34. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬gis_reasoning raises P(spectral_analysis) from 0.34 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.34,0.46
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.6436)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.34)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
